title: The Righteousness of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The righteousness of God means that God always is and does what is right, pure, faithful, and true. His judgments, actions, commands, and saving work are perfectly consistent with His holy character.
summary: The righteousness of God means that God always is and does what is right, pure, faithful, and true. His judgments, actions, commands, and saving work are perfectly consistent with His holy character.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reveals the righteousness of God by living in perfect obedience and by becoming the righteous basis for the justification of sinners. At the cross, God is shown to be both just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God is righteous in Himself. He is not measured by a standard outside Himself, as though righteousness existed above Him. His own holy character is the standard of what is right.

Everything God does is righteous. His commands are right, His judgments are right, His promises are right, and His ways are right even when human beings cannot fully understand them.

The righteousness of God is revealed with special clarity in the Gospel. God does not forgive sinners by ignoring justice. Through Christ’s atoning sacrifice, God upholds righteousness while showing mercy to those who believe.

God’s righteousness also gives His people confidence in confession. He is faithful and righteous to forgive His people and cleanse them because Christ has accomplished redemption.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often accuse God of unfairness when His ways confront their desires or remain beyond their understanding. The righteousness of God anchors believers in the truth that the Lord is upright in all His ways.

This doctrine also protects the Gospel from becoming sentimental. Forgiveness is not God pretending sin does not matter. In Christ, mercy comes through righteousness, not around it.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Trust God’s righteousness when His commands confront you, His timing confuses you, or His judgments sober you. Confess sin honestly, cling to Christ’s righteousness, and seek to walk uprightly because the God who saves you is righteous in all His ways.
